subject: Logic
title: Gödel's Incompleteness
description: A fast breakdown of Gödel's Incompleteness for builders.

hook.text: In 1931, a 25-year-old proved that math can never be complete. Every system has blind spots.

buildup.text: Kurt Gödel showed that in any consistent system, some true statements can't be proven within it.

discovery.text: He constructed a mathematical sentence that says, "This statement cannot be proven." If provable, contradiction.

twist.text: Self-reference strikes again. Gödel used the liar paradox's structure inside arithmetic itself.

climax.text: No formal system can prove all truths about itself. Math has inherent, unavoidable limits.

quiz.question: What did Gödel's incompleteness theorems prove?
options: Some truths can't be proven within their system
